entry_points.text: Base entries cover version and modeset control; memory entries cover GEM close, open, capability query and prime handle exchange.
Legacy entries manage unique, maps, master, contexts, drawables and DMA.
Graphics entries cover AGP acquire, info, scatter-gather alloc, blank wait, controller sequence and drawable update.
Mode entries cover resources, controller set, atomic commits and leases; sync entries cover create and wait.

exports.text: Headers publish stable user ABI for sockets, stats, terminals and DRM via numeric ids and fixed record layouts shared by kernel and user.
Legacy device numbers use unsigned int; signal handling provides handler types with default null and ignore one.

hazards.text: Resource selectors run 0-15 with limit count 16; unlimited marker is all bits set.
Signal origins separate user from kernel; fault groups define ILL, FPE, SEGV and BUS codes.
Trap, child, poll and syscall fault codes plus emulator tags are enumerated; notification selectors cover signal, none, thread and thread id.
Action flags, mask ops, 64-signal numbering with realtime range, and alternate stack sizes are fixed.
Socket level 1 with basic and extended options plus socket ioctls for ownership, queue and old stamp queries.
Higher socket options run 43-85 with filter, pacing, timestamping and device-memory controls; time options have OLD and NEW forms.
Terminal input, output, baud, control, queue, character slots, local and modem bits use fixed masks and numbers.
DRM declares driver name, control ops, mapping flags, vblank types, device, prime and client capabilities, ioctl base, command base and event types.
User pointers with lengths need validation and bounded copy; volatile lock uses contention bits; some mode ioctls are deprecated.

invariants.text: Size aliases have two spellings; offsets and times split by width with extended offsets 64-bit and clock ticks following kernel long.
Signal headers order number, error, code plus details in two variants; arch hooks fix band and clock types; short aliases expose nested fields.
Timestamp option names resolve statically to OLD or dynamically by time_t size, selecting OLD when matching kernel long else NEW.
Statfs words follow kernel long on 64-bit else 32-bit, packing macros default empty; 64-bit swap builds from 32-bit steps; headers guard once.
Terminal scalars use unsigned char for control chars and unsigned int for speeds and flag fields.
Capability get and set share identifier-value width; blank wait reuses one payload both ways; prime and waits pair handles with fds or points.

locks.text: Hardware lock keeps volatile word padded to cache line; acquire modifiers order DMA drain with ready, quiescent, flush or halt before grant.

state_machines.text: Master, contexts, drawables, port memory and syncobjs move from acquire or create through use to release; modeset emits pre notification.

structs.text: Filesystem id holds two ints; 64-bit semaphore and shared-memory descriptors sequence permissions, times, counts with split times on narrow words.
Signal values union int or pointer; extended details union kill, timer, child, fault, poll and syscall; siginfo wraps header plus padding to max size.
Notification events hold value, signal and selector plus thread id or routine; total cap 64 with computed pad.
Signal sets use one long per word; actions pair handler, flags, optional restorer with mask last; alternate stacks bundle pointer, flags and size.
Statfs orders type, sizes, counts, ids and spares; 64-bit forms widen counts while compat fixes words to 32-bit.
Termios stores four flag words, discipline, control array plus speeds in extended forms; winsize holds rows, cols and pixels; ucontext ends with mask.
DRM drawing uses clip rects, version strings by length plus buffer, maps with offset and flags, clients with ids, and stats with typed counters.
DMA exchanges separate outbound and inbound lists with flags and granted count; contexts pair handle and flags; auth carries magic; IRQ routes slot.
Blank wait overlays request and reply; modeset pairs controller and command; AGP reports aperture and bindings; GEM maps names to handles.
Sync objects use handles with timeline points and timeouts; controller queries return active state and time; events start with type and length.
